text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Lagos bids final farewell to Nigeria's first president, Nnamdi Azikiwe, who died in May. His body lay in state in Lagos on Wednesday preparatory to burial in his home in eastern Nigeria on Saturday.
- Federal government may acquire 9.1 billion naira debt owed by state governments and issue bonds to the creditor banks.

- Federal government to set up tribunal to settle cases of oil spillages because of continued disagreement between oil companies and oil communities over payments for pollution caused by such incidents.
- Zaire sends SOS message to Nigeria on situation in that country; military ruler General Sani Abacha canvasses for dialogue to resolve the conflict.
- Thirty four killed, 19 injured in road accident in Kano, northern Nigeria on Tuesday evening.
- Bureaucracy stalls payment of $145 million federal government cash obligations to its oil joint venture partners.
- A Chinese firm is to build two power stations, one in the capital Abuja and the other in the steel town of Ajaokuta, says mines and power minister Bashir Dalhatu.

- Investigations show that military ruler General Sani Abacha has not signed into law any decree authorising government to acquire controlling golden shares in four leading banks as published by another local newspaper last week.
- Petroleum trust Fund set up to use money made from pump price increase to rehabilitate public infrastructure says it earned 3.08 billion naira from its investment of 25.45 billion.
